request.prompt:
Job T02: usp_load_dim_policy. Parameters per run, in order: SnapshotDate=2025-06-30; SnapshotDate=2025-12-31.

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job      : dw.usp_load_dim_policy
  3 |   Purpose  : Policy dimension for finance, actuarial and broker reporting. One
  4 |              row per version of a policy term, with its product, broker and
  5 |              customer segment. A new version starts whenever the status,
  6 |              broker, annual premium or vehicle registration changes from one
  7 |              policy snapshot to the next (type 2 history).
  8 |   Run by   : POL_SNAPSHOT_LOAD, once per policy snapshot, oldest first:
  9 |              EXEC dw.usp_load_dim_policy @SnapshotDate = '<snapshot date>'
 10 |   Output   : dw.dim_policy. Keeps history, so the procedure never truncates
 11 |              it. Deploying this script recreates the table empty: reload every
 12 |              snapshot in date order afterwards.
 13 |   Author   : MOB
 14 | 
 15 |   Change log
 16 |     2014-02-10  MOB   Initial version, one row per policy (CR-0655)
 17 |     2015-06-22  MOB   Broker name from the broker register (CR-0790)
 18 |     2016-09-05  TF    Direct business reported as broker DIRECT-SALES (CR-0961)
 19 |     2017-03-13  TF    Type 2 history with MERGE, surrogate key policy_sk
 20 |                       (CR-1077)
 21 |     2018-10-01  PH    Vehicle registration tracked for motor (CR-1388)
 22 |     2019-07-15  PH    Customer segment from dw.dim_customer (CR-1610)
 23 |     2020-02-03  TF    Refuse a snapshot older than the last one loaded
 24 |                       (INC-2105)
 25 |     2021-06-14  KB    Logging through etl.usp_log_step (CR-2003)
 26 | ==============================================================================*/
 27 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 28 | GO
 29 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'dw.dim_policy', N'U') IS NOT NULL
 30 |     DROP TABLE dw.dim_policy;
 31 | 
 32 | CREATE TABLE dw.dim_policy (
 33 |     policy_sk             INT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
 34 |     policy_id             INT            NOT NULL,
 35 |     policy_number         VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL,
 36 |     customer_id           INT            NOT NULL,
 37 |     customer_segment      CHAR(4)        NULL,
 38 |     product_code          VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
 39 |     product_name          NVARCHAR(60)   NOT NULL,
 40 |     lob_code              VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 41 |     broker_code           VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
 42 |     broker_name           NVARCHAR(80)   NULL,
 43 |     status                VARCHAR(12)    NOT NULL,
 44 |     inception_date        DATE           NOT NULL,
 45 |     expiry_date           DATE           NOT NULL,
 46 |     cancellation_date     DATE           NULL,
 47 |     annual_premium        DECIMAL(12,2)  NOT NULL,
 48 |     currency              CHAR(3)        NOT NULL,
 49 |     vehicle_reg           VARCHAR(12)    NULL,
 50 |     ncd_years             INT            NULL,
 51 |     valid_from            DATE           NOT NULL,
 52 |     valid_to              DATE           NOT NULL,   -- 9999-12-31 while current
 53 |     is_current            CHAR(1)        NOT NULL,   -- Y / N
 54 |     source_snapshot_date  DATE           NOT NULL,
 55 |     load_ts               DATETIME2(3)   NOT NULL,
 56 |     CONSTRAINT pk_dim_policy PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (policy_sk)
 57 | );
 58 | 
 59 | CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX ix_dim_policy_policy_id ON dw.dim_policy (policy_id, is_current);
 60 | GO
 61 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dw.usp_load_dim_policy
 62 |     @SnapshotDate DATE
 63 | AS
 64 | BEGIN
 65 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 66 | 
 67 |     DECLARE @job_name     VARCHAR(128) = 'dw.usp_load_dim_policy',
 68 |             @rows         INT,
 69 |             @closed       INT,
 70 |             @last_loaded  DATE,
 71 |             @err_msg      NVARCHAR(4000),
 72 |             @err_no       INT;
 73 | 
 74 |     BEGIN TRY
 75 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 76 | 
 77 |         /* Oldest snapshot first: loading an older snapshot after a newer one
 78 |            would reopen versions that are already closed (INC-2105) */
 79 |         SELECT  @last_loaded = MAX(d.source_snapshot_date)
 80 |         FROM    dw.dim_policy d;
 81 | 
 82 |         IF @SnapshotDate < @last_loaded
 83 |             THROW 50001, 'dw.dim_policy already holds a later policy snapshot', 1;
 84 | 
 85 |         IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#src') IS NOT NULL DROP TABLE #src;
 86 | 
 87 |         /* 1. This snapshot's policies with product, broker and customer segment */
 88 |         SELECT  p.policy_id,
 89 |                 p.policy_number,
 90 |                 p.customer_id,
 91 |                 c.segment_code                          AS customer_segment,
 92 |                 pr.product_code,
 93 |                 pr.product_name,
 94 |                 pr.lob_code,
 95 |                 ISNULL(p.broker_code, 'DIRECT-SALES')   AS broker_code,
 96 |                 b.broker_name,
 97 |                 p.status,
 98 |                 p.inception_date,
 99 |                 p.expiry_date,
100 |                 p.cancellation_date,
101 |                 p.annual_premium,
102 |                 p.currency,
103 |                 p.vehicle_reg,
104 |                 p.ncd_years
105 |         INTO    #src
106 |         FROM    stg.policy_snapshots p WITH (NOLOCK)
107 |         JOIN    stg.products pr WITH (NOLOCK)
108 |                 ON pr.product_code = p.product_code
109 |         LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK)
110 |                ON b.broker_code = p.broker_code
111 |         LEFT JOIN dw.dim_customer c WITH (NOLOCK)
112 |                ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
113 |         WHERE   p.snapshot_date = @SnapshotDate;
114 | 
115 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
116 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'policy snapshot', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
117 | 
118 |         IF @rows = 0
119 |             THROW 50002, 'No policies found for this snapshot date', 1;
120 | 
121 |         CREATE CLUSTERED INDEX ix_src_policy_id ON #src (policy_id);
122 | 
123 |         BEGIN TRANSACTION;
124 | 
125 |         /* 2. Close the current version of policies whose status, broker, premium
126 |               or vehicle registration has changed since the last snapshot */
127 |         MERGE dw.dim_policy AS tgt
128 |         USING #src AS src
129 |            ON tgt.policy_id = src.policy_id
130 |           AND tgt.is_current = 'Y'
131 |         WHEN MATCHED AND (   ISNULL(src.status, '')        <> ISNULL(tgt.status, '')
132 |                           OR ISNULL(src.broker_code, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.broker_code, '')
133 |                           OR ISNULL(src.annual_premium, 0) <> ISNULL(tgt.annual_premium, 0)
134 |                           OR ISNULL(src.vehicle_reg, '')   <> ISNULL(tgt.vehicle_reg, ''))
135 |         THEN UPDATE
136 |              SET    tgt.valid_to   = DATEADD(DAY, -1, @SnapshotDate),
137 |                     tgt.is_current = 'N';
138 | 
139 |         SET @closed = @@ROWCOUNT;
140 | 
141 |         /* 3. Open a current version for new policies and for those closed above */
142 |         INSERT INTO dw.dim_policy
143 |                (policy_id, policy_number, customer_id, customer_segment, product_code,
144 |                 product_name, lob_code, broker_code, broker_name, status, inception_date,
145 |                 expiry_date, cancellation_date, annual_premium, currency, vehicle_reg,
146 |                 ncd_years, valid_from, valid_to, is_current, source_snapshot_date, load_ts)
147 |         SELECT  s.policy_id, s.policy_number, s.customer_id, s.customer_segment, s.product_code,
148 |                 s.product_name, s.lob_code, s.broker_code, s.broker_name, s.status,
149 |                 s.inception_date, s.expiry_date, s.cancellation_date, s.annual_premium,
150 |                 s.currency, s.vehicle_reg, s.ncd_years,
151 |                 @SnapshotDate,
152 |                 '9999-12-31',
153 |                 'Y',
154 |                 @SnapshotDate,
155 |                 SYSDATETIME()
156 |         FROM    #src s
157 |         WHERE   NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1
158 |                             FROM   dw.dim_policy d
159 |                             WHERE  d.policy_id = s.policy_id
160 |                               AND  d.is_current = 'Y')
161 |         ORDER BY s.policy_id;
162 | 
163 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
164 | 
165 |         COMMIT TRANSACTION;
166 | 
167 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions closed', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @closed;
168 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'versions opened', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
169 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
170 |     END TRY
171 |     BEGIN CATCH
172 |         IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
173 | 
174 |         SELECT  @err_msg = ERROR_MESSAGE(),
175 |                 @err_no  = ERROR_NUMBER();
176 | 
177 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job_name, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
178 |              @message = @err_msg, @error_number = @err_no;
179 |         THROW;
180 |     END CATCH
181 | END;
182 | GO

Input tables:
- stg.policy_snapshots: snapshot_date DATE NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, policy_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, broker_code VARCHAR(10), inception_date DATE NOT NULL, expiry_date DATE NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, cancellation_date DATE, annual_premium DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, sum_insured DECIMAL(14,2), payment_frequency VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, vehicle_reg VARCHAR(12), ncd_years INT
- stg.brokers: broker_code CHAR(6) NOT NULL, broker_name NVARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, region VARCHAR(20), commission_rate DECIMAL(5,4) NOT NULL, status VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, appointed_date DATE NOT NULL
- stg.products: product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, product_name NVARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, lob_code VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL, term_months INT, levy_rate DECIMAL(5,4) NOT NULL, launched_on DATE NOT NULL, withdrawn_on DATE
- dw.dim_customer: customer_id INT NOT NULL, first_name NVARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, last_name NVARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, full_name NVARCHAR(101) NOT NULL, initials NVARCHAR(2) NOT NULL, email VARCHAR(120), email_shared_count INT NOT NULL, date_of_birth DATE, age_at_join INT, address_line1 NVARCHAR(100), town NVARCHAR(50), county VARCHAR(30), region VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, eircode VARCHAR(10), eircode_valid CHAR(1) NOT NULL, segment_code CHAR(4), is_standard_segment CHAR(1) NOT NULL, marketing_opt_in CHAR(1) NOT NULL, customer_since DATE NOT NULL, source_system VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, version_count INT NOT NULL, record_updated_at DATETIME2(0) NOT NULL, as_of_date DATE NOT NULL
- dw.dim_policy: policy_sk INT NOT NULL, policy_id INT NOT NULL, policy_number VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, customer_id INT NOT NULL, customer_segment CHAR(4), product_code VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, product_name NVARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, lob_code VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL, broker_code VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, broker_name NVARCHAR(80), status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL, inception_date DATE NOT NULL, expiry_date DATE NOT NULL, cancellation_date DATE, annual_premium DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL, currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL, vehicle_reg VARCHAR(12), ncd_years INT, valid_from DATE NOT NULL, valid_to DATE NOT NULL, is_current CHAR(1) NOT NULL, source_snapshot_date DATE NOT NULL, load_ts DATETIME2(3) NOT NULL

Semantic traps to test (one case per distinct trap id):
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 37-37: customer_segment is CHAR(4), copied from CHAR(4) segment_code, so legacy values are padded to 4 characters. Spark strings never pad, so shorter codes come out without trailing spaces.
- TSQL-06 (ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks) at lines 95-95: ISNULL takes the type of p.broker_code, which is VARCHAR(10), so 'DIRECT-SALES' (12 chars) is cut to 'DIRECT-SAL'. A Spark coalesce would write the full literal.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 107-108: The product join compares VARCHAR product_code values case-insensitively, so case variants still match. A Spark join drops them, and with them the policy row, because this is an inner join.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 107-108: The product_code join ignores trailing spaces. In Spark, a code with trailing spaces fails the inner join and the policy is lost.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 109-110: The broker join on text matches case variants under the CI collation. A Spark binary join misses them, so broker_name is NULL.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 109-110: stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6) and gets padded, while policy broker_code is VARCHAR(10). SQL Server ignores the padding when matching. In Spark the padded values do not match, so broker_name becomes NULL.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 131-131: The status <> check is case-insensitive, so a change of letter case only (e.g. 'Active' to 'ACTIVE') opens no new version in legacy. Spark would open one.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 131-131: The status <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a change in trailing spaces alone does not close the version in legacy.
- TSQL-06 (ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks) at lines 131-131: The status change check uses ISNULL(..., ''), so a NULL status and '' count as equal and no new version opens.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 132-132: The broker_code <> check is case-insensitive, so a broker code that changes only in letter case does not trigger a new version in legacy.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 132-132: The broker_code <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a code that differs only by trailing spaces does not count as a change.
- TSQL-06 (ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks) at lines 132-132: The broker_code change check treats NULL and '' as the same value. Also, the source side has already been truncated to 'DIRECT-SAL' by the ISNULL at line 95, and Spark must compare against that truncated value.
- TSQL-06 (ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks) at lines 133-133: ISNULL(annual_premium, 0) treats a NULL premium and 0 as equal, so that difference opens no new version.
- TSQL-01 (Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins) at lines 134-134: The vehicle_reg <> check is case-insensitive, so a registration that changes only in case ('ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE') is not a change in legacy.
- TSQL-02 (Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces) at lines 134-134: The vehicle_reg <> check ignores trailing spaces, so a registration with added trailing spaces is not seen as changed.
- TSQL-06 (ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks) at lines 134-134: vehicle_reg is nullable. ISNULL(..., '') makes NULL and '' equal, so moving between NULL and empty opens no new version. Spark null-safe comparisons would treat it as a change.
request.system_prompt:
You are the test author agent of LANSH, a factory that migrates legacy T-SQL (SQL Server 2022) jobs to PySpark and must reproduce their output exactly. For each semantic trap you are given, write one small input set (5 to 20 rows per table) on which a naive translation of this job would give a different result from the legacy engine, while the job still produces output rows.

- Use only the job's input tables and their columns; respect each column's legacy type and length (a VARCHAR(5) value has at most 5 characters) and fill every NOT NULL column.
- Write every value as text: dates YYYY-MM-DD, datetimes YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, numbers as plain decimals; use null for NULL. Leave _row_seq out: the rows' order is their _row_seq.
- Include the related rows the job needs to produce output (for example, a claim's payments) and rows on both sides of the trap (the variant that a naive translation mishandles, and the canonical value).
- The expected output is computed by running the legacy job itself on your rows, so never state expected values.

cases.description: Letter-case variants across two runs (2025-06-30, then 2025-12-31). Policy 1001 has product_code 'motor01' and the product register has 'MOTOR01'. The legacy inner join still matches it; a binary Spark join drops the policy. Policy 1002 has broker 'brk001' and the register has 'BRK001'. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark leaves it NULL. In run 2 the changes are case-only: 1001 status 'Active' to 'ACTIVE', 1002 broker 'brk001' to 'BRK001', 1003 vehicle_reg 'ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE'. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would close and reopen each one. Policy 1004 is the control: its status really changes, to 'Lapsed'.

Trailing spaces and CHAR padding across two runs. Policy 2001 has product_code 'MOTOR01 ' with a trailing space. The legacy inner join keeps it; Spark drops the policy. Its broker 'BRK1' matches the CHAR(6) register code 'BRK1  ', which is stored padded. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark gets NULL. Customers 501 and 503 have CHAR(4) segment codes 'GO' and 'STD', which legacy pads to 'GO  ' and 'STD '; Spark leaves them unpadded. Customer 502's 'PLAT' is the canonical 4-character code. In run 2 the only changes are trailing spaces: 2001 status 'Active  ', 2002 broker 'BRK002 ', 2003 vehicle_reg 'CD34EFG  '. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would. Policy 2004 is the control: its premium really changes.

ISNULL behaviour across two runs. Policies 3001 and 3004 (run 1) and 3005 (new in run 2) have a NULL broker_code. ISNULL takes the VARCHAR(10) type of p.broker_code, so legacy stores 'DIRECT-SAL'; a Spark coalesce writes 'DIRECT-SALES'. 3001 stays NULL in run 2. Legacy compares 'DIRECT-SAL' with 'DIRECT-SAL' and opens no version. A Spark job that compares the full literal against the stored value, or that mixes the two, can flag a change. 3002 moves vehicle_reg from NULL to '', and 3003 from '' to NULL. Under ISNULL(...,'') these are equal and no version opens; a null-safe Spark compare would open one. 3004 is the control: its broker really changes, from NULL to BRK001. NULL status or premium cannot be tested here because both columns are NOT NULL in staging.
